channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: What it’s like to dine inside Eat Street restaurants right now
item.description: You’ll find the food and hospitality one would expect from the Nicollet Avenue restaurants we know and love, with one caveat: Everyone is hurting.

item.title: Tired of living in fear, this family decided to deport themselves
item.description: An immigrant family from Ecuador said they felt like prisoners in their Minneapolis home.

item.title: Minnesota to visit thousands of providers in fraud-fighting push
item.description: The state is checking on service providers in push to rebuild trust and prevent the federal government from withholding funds.

item.title: Why the Trump administration keeps asking for Minnesota’s welfare data
item.description: Vice President JD Vance said the information could facilitate immigration enforcement. Legal experts say that’s a drastic overreach of federal power.

item.title: Minnesota’s big election year begins: What to know about 2026 precinct caucuses
item.description: Precinct caucuses Feb. 3 kick off an election year that could reshape leadership of Minnesota.

item.title: After 9 days, Hennepin County medical examiner classifies Alex Pretti’s death as ‘homicide’
item.description: Homicide means the death came at the hands of another person and does not necessarily mean the person died from a criminal act.

item.title: Minnesota prosecutors formally demand evidence from Trump administration over the killing of Renee Good
item.description: The Hennepin County Attorney’s Office said it has sent what are known as Touhy letters to gain crime scene evidence from the shooting death of Renee Good by ICE agent Jonathan Ross.

item.title: Federal order reinstates unannounced congressional visits to ICE detention facilities
item.description: Members of Congress filed a lawsuit after they were not allowed to inspect conditions at the Whipple Federal Building where detainees have described inhumane treatment.

item.title: The latest: All DHS agents in Minnesota to be outfitted with body cameras, Noem says
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem says cameras will be provided to federal agents.

item.title: Another wave of departures in Minnesota’s U.S. Attorney’s Office
item.description: 14 attorneys have left this year, which prosecutors are calling unprecedented.
